content_voiceover: This slide catalogs the specific NCCN-preferred drug regimens for ATLL, split into initial and second-line therapy. For initial therapy, the preferred options are CHP, that's cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone, combined with brentuximab vedotin for CD30 positive cases; CHOP plus mogamulizumab when transplant isn't planned; dose-adjusted EPOCH; or interferon plus zidovudine for the acute, chronic, and symptomatic smoldering subtypes. Other recommended options include CHOEP and hyper-CVAD alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine, and plain CHOP is reserved for patients who can't tolerate more intensive regimens or who lack CD30 expression. For second-line or subsequent therapy, preferred options are single agents like brentuximab vedotin for CD30 positive disease, lenalidomide, or mogamulizumab, or combination regimens borrowed from aggressive lymphoma salvage protocols: platinum-based regimens like DHA plus platinum, ESHA plus platinum, GDP, GemOx, GVD, and ICE. Alternative second-line options include alemtuzumab, arsenic trioxide, belinostat, bendamustine, gemcitabine, pralatrexate, and localized radiation for symptomatic disease. The key takeaway for boards is that brentuximab vedotin's role is tied specifically to CD30 expression, and that mogamulizumab, an anti-CCR4 antibody, is a T-cell lymphoma-specific option that shouldn't be used if allogeneic transplant is planned, because of graft-versus-host disease risk.
keypoints: Preferred initial: CHP+brentuximab vedotin (CD30+), CHOP+mogamulizumab, dose-adjusted EPOCH
Interferon/zidovudine for acute, chronic, and symptomatic smoldering subtypes
Second-line: brentuximab vedotin, lenalidomide, mogamulizumab, or platinum-based salvage (DHA, ESHA, GDP, ICE)
Brentuximab vedotin reserved for CD30-positive disease
Avoid mogamulizumab if allogeneic transplant is planned (GVHD risk)
keypoint_voiceover: Two drugs to flag for boards. Brentuximab vedotin is added specifically for CD30 positive ATLL, in both first and second line. Mogamulizumab, the anti-CCR4 antibody, is used when transplant isn't intended, because it raises graft-versus-host disease risk if given before allogeneic transplant. Otherwise initial therapy is CHOP-based or dose-adjusted EPOCH, and second-line borrows platinum-based salvage regimens like DHA, ESHA, GDP, and ICE from aggressive lymphoma protocols.
